title: Output Schema & Function-Call Behavior: Acceptance Criteria and Failure Modes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria for structured output (JSON/typed payloads) and function/tool-calling behavior across synchronous and streaming modes. This ticket captures the contract guarantees, error modes, downgrade/fallback behavior, and QA matrix so engineering, SDKs, and QA can implement consistent tests and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Synchronous structured responses must either return a final JSON payload that validates against the declared schema OR return a well-formed error object that includes error_type, message, and optional diagnostic hints.

Streaming structured output (chunked) must produce chunks that concatenate to a final payload that validates against the declared schema. Each chunk must be a parseable JSON prefix per the streaming framing rules documented in the PRD.

Tool/function call tokens must be surfaced as a typed 'tool_call' envelope in the output with fields: name (string), version (optional string), args (JSON object), and confidence (optional numeric). The envelope schema must be stable for SDKs to consume.

When the model emits a tool_call during streaming, SDKs should be able to detect the call intent before the final chunk; server must publish a deterministic event with call id, name, and partial args so downstream orchestrators can prepare resources (e.g., open socket, reserve external API quota).

Schema mismatch behavior: if the final payload fails validation, the API must return HTTP 200 with body indicating validation_failed=true and include 'validation_errors' list. For high-severity validation failures (missing required top-level fields), server must log as customer-impacting and return guidance in the response for remediation.

Fallbacks: if a model variant does not support structured output or fails repeatedly, the routing policy must trigger a compatible fallback variant (same schema) or return a clear 'structured_output_unavailable' error and optional 'suggested_action' (e.g., retry after upgrade or use unstructured mode).

Partial streaming errors: if an error occurs mid-stream (compute/node failure, encoding error), the server must emit an 'error_chunk' with error_code and position_hint, continue to close the stream gracefully, and include final metadata explaining whether a retry is safe and whether the partial payload can be used.

Determinism for tool selection: for prompts that might map to multiple tools, server must expose the model's decision rationale (short token-level reason) in telemetry and optionally in a 'tool_choice' field for auditability. Acceptance requires a sample prompt and deterministic tool selection across 5 repeated runs in test harness.

SDK compatibility: JS, Python, and Go SDKs must include helpers to parse streamable tool_call envelopes, rehydrate partial args, and surface canonical errors. Acceptance requires passing SDK integration tests that consume a synthetic streaming output and successfully invoke a mock tool with reconstructed args.

Observability: every structured output and tool_call must emit tracing spans with tags: request_id, model_family, variant, schema_id, tool_name (if any), and validation_result. Acceptance requires a dashboard widget that shows validation failure rate by model variant and schema_id.

Backwards compatibility: the final envelope shape must be backwards compatible with previously shipped minimal structured-output responses. Any breaking change must be gated behind a feature flag and documented in the migration guide.

Security: tool_call args must never include secrets in cleartext. Acceptance requires a static analyzer test that rejects schemas with fields named like password/secret/api_key unless flagged with 'sensitive:true' and KMS integration is present in the request metadata.

Performance: structured output streaming must not increase median end-to-end latency by more than 8% for 95th percentile payloads compared to unstructured streaming baseline in the same variant. Acceptance requires benchmark reports attached to the ticket.

Error codes and retry semantics: define canonical error_code list (e.g., schema_validation_error, tool_unavailable, stream_truncated, fallback_triggered) and map each to recommended client retry behavior (no-retry, immediate-retry, backoff). Acceptance contains a table of codes and retry guidance in attachments.

Manual review mode: when 'require_manual_review' flag is set for a schema, any tool_call must be paused with state 'awaiting_review' and include a reviewer_link. Acceptance requires an end-to-end test that triggers pause and resumes after a simulated approval action.
test_matrix: E2E: streaming + tool_call + successful schema validation across 3 model families (llama-3, mixtral, redwood-rl).
E2E: streaming + mid-stream node failure -> verify error_chunk emitted and client can detect retryable=false for partial payloads.
SDK: reconstruct tool_call args in JS/Python/Go and invoke mock tool; assert idempotency and argument parity.
Compatibility: legacy clients receive clear validation_failed envelope and non-breaking response shape.
Security: schema containing 'password' field flagged and request rejected unless KMS header present.
Performance: run 1000 sample requests to measure latency delta and token throughput impact.

notes: This ticket is intended to be the canonical acceptance checklist used by engineering and QA for the structured-output rollout. It intentionally enumerates both happy-path behaviors and non-happy-path error modes so SDKs and orchestration layers can be tested thoroughly.
